chapter: Tropicana, Bebo Valdes and the batanga
title: Bebo Valdes and the batanga rhythm
summary: Batanga, created by Bebo in 1952 on Cadena Azul, combined conga and bata drums; it succeeded as music but not as a dance, despite Fellove's efforts.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: At that time is when I understand that Bebo Valdés came out with a new rhythm called...

Yes, it was the combination of the conga and bata drums and very good arrangements. It began in 1952 on radio Cadena Azul. The rhythm Batanga. And Bebo was the composer and creator and the contributors were Trinidad Torregrosa who played the Iyá batá drum, Rolando Alfonso, Jesus and me. We were the . . . the rhthym section of Bebo Valdés’ Orquesta Ritmo de Batanga.
And what kind of popularity did the Batanga have?
Musically yes, but it was hard to put a dance to it. That was why . . .
Why so? I don't get it . . .

Because the steps, if I can say bluntly, the steps were difficult for some people so then it continued only as music. The music continued with great success. Fellove was the one who tried to give it dance steps. Because when we did the broadcasts every Sunday, while the orchestra played Fellove began to teach the audience the steps and stuff, but dancing alone is different than dancing with a partner. Because alone you can do anything you want, but with a partner it’s different and it was not easy for the partner to follow the steps of the lead dancer. That's why the dance was not very successful. But the music itself, yes. Several orchestras recorded his music here with the rhythm of Batanga with bata drums - African drums.
